thread:
jeff: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need a concrete plan for per-route identity fallbacks. Today some infra routes implicitly accept org keys when project keys are missing. We should decide guardrails

anita: +1 we saw a production incident where a missing project key silently used an org key and misattributed usage. not great.

sarah: Can we outline acceptable fallback hierarchy first? e.g., project-key -> service-account-token -> org-key (only if explicit allowlist)

mike: That ordering makes sense. main tradeoffs: least-privilege vs availability. fallback to org-key expands blast radius.

jeff: Agreed. Proposal: fallbacks are allowed only when a route is marked "fallback-enabled" in route config. Default = false.

lena: How do we audit when fallback happens? need traceability + alerts.

anita: Logging: every fallback should emit a structured event with original requested actor, chosen credential, and whether consented by route config. Also increment a metric (auth.fallback.count).

jeff: Sounds good. Also require a TTL window for fallback tokens usage? e.g., if project key missing, use a short-lived service token (5m) instead of long-lived org key.

mike: Implementation detail: we have two mechanism patterns: 1) shim that mints ephemeral service token scoped to route OR 2) allow org-key usage but limited to read-only scopes. Both have pros/cons.

anita: I'd lean to ephemeral minting from broker (pattern 1). Keeps long-lived keys out of runtime path and enforces least privilege. But requires broker availability and low-latency.

jeff: If we go ephemeral, we need fallback circuit-breakers: if broker is down, we should fail fast (no silent org-key fallback). Ops wins here.

sarah: Migration plan idea: start with deny-by-default. Then a short canary where selected routes enable fallback-enabled and use ephemeral minting. Monitor auth.fallback.count and erroneous-attribution rate.

lena: Add an annotation to route configs that includes "allowed_fallback_types": ["ephemeral", "org_key"] so we can toggle per-route. Default empty.

mike: Also need RBAC mapping: ephemeral tokens should inherit the original project-level permissions if available, else a minimized safe role. We should avoid grant-everything.

jeff: API changes: SDKs should get a clear error code when project key missing (AUTH_NO_PROJECT_KEY) and a header X-Fallback-Used when fallback happens. We can use header for quick filtering.

anita: +1 on header. Also require that any route using org_key fallback must have an explicit audit exception in vault and a quarterly review.

ops-bot: Reminder: canary rollout scheduled 2024-10-03 02:00 UTC. Ensure instrumented metrics are in datadog.auth.fallback.*

jeff: Action items: 1) eng-svc-auth to implement ephemeral mint path + circuit-breaker (mike) 2) platform to add route config fields and validation (lena) 3) sdk/clients: map new error codes & header (sarah) 4) security to draft org-key exception process (anita).

mike: I'll PR an initial implementation for the broker minting shim. Will include a config flag `fallback.enabled` and `fallback.allowed_types` in route manifest.

anita: We'll prepare the audit doc and deprecation timeline for org-key fallback (90-day window once ephemeral available).

jeff: Good. Anyone opposed to this approach?

sarah: No objections. Sounds safe. :thumbsup:

lena: ok, i'll add validation to the route linter and make it fail CI if unknown fallback types are used.

jeff: Great. We'll sync next week for PR reviews. Closing the thread for now.
